findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the ≥95% fingerprint-verified target: either make child 471c (or 4bd8) assert ≥95% as a gate, or amend parent AC1 to state the observed-ratio-informs-a-floor policy the children actually implement.
evidence: Parent AC1: '...fingerprint-verified for ≥95% of v2 sidecars; verified by the corpus manifest's coverage counts.'

Child 471c AC2: 'no threshold is asserted as a hard gate in this ticket — the observed ratio from the real build is the input the epic's later noise-floor/label work (expectable-clownlike-ynambu) uses to decide whether a floor is warranted'
Child 4bd8 (expectable-clownlike-ynambu) only computes labels/noise floor from whatever ratio exists; it does not gate on ≥95% either.
findings.finding: Parent AC1 requires at-review plan text fingerprint-verified for ≥95% of v2 sidecars as a completion gate, but child 471c explicitly refuses to assert any verification threshold ('no threshold is asserted as a hard gate in this ticket'), and no sibling enforces the ≥95% bar. The parent's observable outcome is therefore not delivered by the roster.
scenarios: Real build reconstructs plan text for only, say, 88% of v2 sidecars: child 471c passes its own ACs (it reports verified_ratio) but the epic-level AC1 (≥95%) is unmet and no child fails.
Completion verifier checks parent AC1 against children and finds the ≥95% observable outcome owned by nobody.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend parent AC1 to match the children's design (report verified_ratio; a warranted-floor decision follows) OR add an explicit ≥95% gate to child 471c's acceptance criteria so some sibling owns the parent's bar.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the noise-band computation: which metric(s) it applies to, how the identical-material flip rate and Tier-1 reproduction agreement combine, and the numeric/confidence rule for 'exceeds the band'.
evidence: Invariant 4: 'reported as regressing/improving only when its label-proxy deltas exceed the noise band measured from identical-material flips and the Tier-1 reproduction run; otherwise "indistinguishable".'

Two inputs are named (208 identical-material verdict flips; the Tier-1 reproduction-run agreement) but the plan never states how they are combined into a single band, on which metric, or at what confidence.
findings.finding: The 'noise band' that governs the load-bearing acceptance rule (invariant 4) is a derived metric with no stated computation or aggregation protocol.
findings.location: Approach invariant 4 (Noise-aware acceptance); Acceptance Criteria (Tier-1 noise floor)
scenarios: An executor must decide how to turn 208 flips + a per-question agreement rate into a numeric threshold for 'exceeds the noise band' and has no defined method — they would stop to ask, or invent an arbitrary rule.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the model-id comparison rule for the parity guard: state the normalization applied to `provider_provenance.ran_model` (e.g. canonical model-class token vs. raw string vs. prefix match) that both the diff-refusal and the start-time baseline check use.
evidence: Plan: 'refuses to diff runs whose per-pass model ids differ, and refuses to start when the configured model differs from the corpus baseline's `provider_provenance.ran_model`'
runner.py:483 records `ran_model` as the PROVIDER-QUALIFIED string actually invoked ('the provider-qualified string actually invoked … not the bare config model')

tests/unit/test_llm_fallback_chain.py:303 asserts `ran_model` can end with a `-no-temperature` suffix; fixtures show forms like `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` — region prefixes, inference-profile qualifiers, and dated point-releases all vary within one class
ABSENCE: the plan never states whether the guard compares raw strings, a normalized model-class token, or a prefix — the decision rule the parity check depends on is undefined
findings.finding: The model-parity guard references equality on `provider_provenance.ran_model` but never defines the normalization / 'same model class' rule the executor must apply; `ran_model` is a provider-qualified string that legitimately varies within one model class.
findings.location: Approach → Invariant 2 (Model parity); AC line 'Every eval result records the per-pass model id; the harness refuses to diff results with differing model ids and refuses to run a pass on a model other than its production class'
scenarios: A Bedrock inference-profile ARN or a region-prefixed id for the same Sonnet class differs byte-for-byte from the corpus baseline, so the guard refuses to start a legitimate parity run.

findings.suggested_fix: Specify a canonical `model_class` token derived from `ran_model` (provider + base model family, stripping region/inference-profile qualifiers and the `-no-temperature` suffix) and state that the parity guard compares that token, not the raw `ran_model` string.

findings.location: Approach → Invariant 4 (Noise-aware acceptance); AC lines for Tier-0/Tier-1 reports (label-proxy precision/recall, per-question agreement, noise floor)
scenarios: Two implementers compute the 'indistinguishable' verdict differently — one treats the identical-material flip rate as the band for verdict flips only, another applies it to precision/recall deltas — yielding contradictory accept/reject calls on the same proposal.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the write contract for the manifest-hash-keyed labels file where the Tier-1 reproduction (53ab) records the Pass-2 noise floor into 4bd8's artifact (append vs separate file, hash preservation).

Child 53ab AC: 'The reproduction run (current questions) is recorded with its per-question agreement as the Pass-2 noise floor; checked by the report and the labels file.'
Parent invariant #4 folds identical-material flips AND the Tier-1 reproduction run into one noise band.
findings.finding: The labels artifact is written by two children with no defined merge contract: child 4bd8 emits `labels-<manifest-hash>.jsonl` with the identical-material noise floor (zero LLM), while child 53ab states its Tier-1 reproduction-run per-question agreement 'is stored with the labels' — i.e. a later LLM-run child writes the Pass-2 verifier noise floor back into 4bd8's file. Neither child defines who owns appending/merging the Pass-2 floor into the manifest-hash-keyed labels file.
scenarios: 4bd8 computes and publishes the noise floor first (its own AC), locking the labels file to the manifest hash; 53ab then must mutate that same file to add the Pass-2 reproduction agreement, but 4bd8's loader 'refuses a mismatched pair' — the append must preserve the hash key and no child specifies the append/versioning semantics.
Two commissioning runs of 53ab produce two Pass-2 floor values; unclear which the labels file should hold.
findings.suggested_fix: Have 4bd8 define the labels-file schema with an explicit slot for a later-written Pass-2 reproduction floor, and have 53ab write to that slot rather than mutating the label rows; document the update path in one place.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the Bedrock prompt-caching capability assertion per pass: scope the 'caching confirmed active' AC to the Sonnet (Pass-2/Tier-1) pass only, and re-derive the Tier-2 (Opus) cost estimate assuming NO caching (full input billed per call), citing the measured us./global. opus-4-5 non-caching result.
evidence: infra/runbooks/bedrock-access.md:146-147: 'Measured working: us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6. Measured NOT caching: us./global. claude-opus-4-5-…'
tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py:8: 'us. AND global. opus-4-5 report cache_read=0 AND cache_write=0 while billing the full … input tokens — caching fails SILENTLY and is model-dependent.'

tests/unit/test_cache_floor_warning.py:75 and ADR 0059 §10: opus-4-5 on Bedrock does not cache; 'Bedrock does not straightforwardly fix the opus caching failure … opus-4-5 datapoint is never reconciled.'
findings.finding: The plan assumes Bedrock prompt caching is active for every pass and prices Pass-1 (Opus) and the 'caching confirmed active' AC on that basis, but repo evidence measured against real AWS shows Bedrock opus-4-5 (us./global.) does NOT cache — it reports cache_read=0/cache_write=0 and bills the full input on every call.
findings.location: Invariant 2 'Model parity' (frontier Opus for Pass 1 via Bedrock); Approach Tier-2 '~$3.4/review uncached'; Acceptance Criteria 'Prompt caching is confirmed active for eval runs (cache_read_tokens > 0 on the second call of a run)'
scenarios: The 'cache_read_tokens > 0 on the second call' AC is run against a Tier-2 (Opus) eval and fails permanently because Opus-on-Bedrock cannot cache, blocking the AC.
The Tier-2 baseline sample costs materially more than the ~$3.4/review estimate because every Opus call bills full input, eroding the $200 cap / $30 reserve headroom.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the caching AC by pass (require cache_read>0 only for Sonnet/Tier-1), and either recompute the Tier-2 Opus budget as full-input-per-call or name a caching-capable Opus model id and cite a measurement that it caches on Bedrock before relying on it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the specific historical threshold change and its documented effect (with the source doc) that the Tier-0 reproduction test must replay, and the tolerance for 'reproducing' it.
evidence: AC3: '...verified by replaying current code against itself with zero diffs and replaying a known historical threshold change reproducing its documented effect.'
No specific historical change, its 'documented effect', or the doc it is recorded in is identified.
findings.finding: AC3's verification 'replaying a known historical threshold change reproducing its documented effect' names no specific change, making the criterion non-deterministically evaluable.
scenarios: A reviewer checking AC3 cannot tell which change to replay or what pass/fail delta counts as 'reproducing its documented effect'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that Tier-0 replay and the zero-diff self-check SEGMENT the corpus by IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION (never pool across cohorts), and scope the 'zero diffs' AC to the current-version segment (with off-version sidecars either excluded or diffed only against their own-version scores).
evidence: Plan: 'Re-run review_kernel.decide.pass3_decide … over the whole corpus … diff against stored decisions'
Plan corpus window: '2026-06-27 → now', ~4,300 v2 sidecars
sidecar.py:40-45: IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION stamped so replay can 'SEGMENT old-formula vs new-formula findings and never pool across versions'; current value 'plan-v5'
docs/.../runs/README.md:342 shows plan-v3 was live; fixtures reference plan-v2 — the corpus is multi-version
ADR 0036/0054: a version bump closes the cohort; the old corpus 'cannot be replayed against the new model's scores'
findings.finding: Tier-0 replay 'over the whole corpus' and the AC 'replaying current code against itself with zero diffs' will not hold across the corpus because it spans multiple IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION cohorts (plan-v2 → plan-v5), whose stored impact/priority/decision were produced by different Pass-3 formulas; the codebase's own no-pooling discipline forbids comparing current scores against off-version stored scores.
findings.location: Approach → 'Tier 0 — Pass-3 replay'; Acceptance Criteria (Pass-3 change bullet: 'replaying current code against itself with zero diffs')
scenarios: Author runs the self-vs-self zero-diff check over all v2 sidecars and sees non-zero diffs on every pre-v5 finding, mistaking version artifacts for a harness bug or a regression signal
A Pass-3 formula change is scored over pooled cohorts, inflating or masking the true blast radius
findings.suggested_fix: Add IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION as a required corpus-manifest dimension; Tier-0 groups by version, replays each finding only against the formula that produced it, and the self-vs-self zero-diff AC is asserted per-cohort (current plan-v5 segment), matching sidecar.py's no-pool rule and ADR 0036/0054.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define model parity per-pass-and-per-baseline-sidecar (each re-run must match the specific sidecar it replays / its cohort's ran_model), not against one global corpus baseline, and state how model-pin transitions across the corpus window are handled.
evidence: Plan: harness 'refuses to start when the configured model differs from the corpus baseline's provider_provenance.ran_model' — singular baseline
Corpus window '2026-06-27 → now' + ~4,300 sidecars implies multiple production model pins

compose comments describe a Bedrock 'cutover' and pinned ids (REBAR_LLM_FRONTIER_MODEL / _STANDARD_MODEL) that change over time — provider_provenance.ran_model is per-run and heterogeneous across the window
findings.finding: The model-parity invariant assumes a SINGLE corpus baseline model ('the corpus baseline's provider_provenance.ran_model'), but a corpus spanning ~a year of production carries multiple model pins, so the start-refusal check is either unsatisfiable or silently discards most of the corpus.
scenarios: Tier-1/Tier-2 reproduction run is refused because the current pinned Sonnet/Opus id differs from some older sidecar's ran_model in the sample
The harness silently limits the usable Tier-2 stratified sample to only tickets whose ran_model matches today's pin, biasing the sample and shrinking coverage
findings.suggested_fix: Reframe invariant #2: the refusal compares the configured per-pass model against the ran_model of the specific sidecar(s) being replayed (or that sidecar's version-cohort baseline). Record the model-id distribution in the manifest, and for Tier-2 sampling, either stratify within each model cohort or restrict the sample to the current pin and say so explicitly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile Tier-1/Tier-2 (LLM re-runs) against ADR 0054 §2's rejection of purpose-built LLM eval suites and bulk re-review sweeps — invoke ADR 0054's §2 'evals for their own purposes' carve-out (this is an instrument, not a per-change calibration), and state why the tiers are not the rejected category.
evidence: ADR 0054 §2: 'The following MUST NOT be required, planned, or commissioned … Purpose-built LLM eval suites built for a single calibration question. Bulk re-review sweeps — re-running review-plan / review-code across a corpus of tickets to observe how a candidate value would have scored.'
The plan invokes ADR 0054 as SUPPORT ('Consistent with ADR 0054') but only for Tier 0; Tier 1/2 are bulk LLM re-runs.

ADR 0054 §2 last paragraph DOES carve out 'evals used for their own purposes (prompt development, regression pinning of model behavior, capability checks)' and the existing ab_impact_model.py — a reconciliation path the plan does not invoke.
findings.finding: The plan's Tier-1 (re-run the verifier over the corpus) and Tier-2 (re-run finders over a sample) are precisely the 'purpose-built LLM eval suite' and 'bulk re-review sweep' categories that ADR 0054 §2 explicitly REJECTS, yet the plan cites ADR 0054 only as support for its offline-first/Tier-0 stance and never reconciles the LLM tiers against that rejection.
findings.location: Approach — 'Tier 1 — Pass-2 replay', 'Tier 2 — Pass-1 replay'; Invariant 3 'Offline first … Consistent with ADR 0054'
scenarios: A reviewer or the ADR-0054 author reads the epic as directly contradicting an Accepted ADR the epic itself cites, and blocks it on governance grounds.
The commissioning Tier-1/Tier-2 spend (≤$120) is exactly the 'most expensive part of a calibration' ADR 0054 warns against, absent an explicit carve-out argument.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a paragraph (and a line in the ADR this epic ships) explicitly citing ADR 0054 §2's carve-out for 'regression pinning of model behavior / capability checks', framing Tier-1/2 as building a standing instrument (not gating a single calibration value), and bounding when a Tier-1/2 run is permitted vs when Tier-0 alone suffices.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the epic's ADR, briefly survey external LLM-as-judge eval / judge-reliability prior art (e.g. judge-reliability harnesses, record/replay eval frameworks) and justify the field-corpus noise-band approach vs those established methods.
evidence: Retrieved via web search (DuckDuckGo): an open-source 'Judge Reliability Harness' (arxiv.org/html/2603.05399v1; openreview.net/forum?id=hajH5OBXF8) for stress-testing LLM-judge reliability under perturbations; production LLM-as-judge eval harnesses auditing prompt/version changes against a gold set with record/replay CI (github.com/SGajjar24/llm-eval-harness, github.com/mrjunos/llm-eval-harness).
The plan's noise band from identical-material verdict flips (208) is a judge-reliability measurement; the plan does not reference any established judge-reliability methodology.
findings.finding: The plan builds LLM-judge-style grader tiers and a 'reviewer-noise floor', but considers only in-repo antecedents and does not situate its approach against the established external prior art on LLM-as-judge eval harnesses and judge-reliability/noise measurement.
findings.location: Approach (Tier 1/Tier 2 as graders); Invariant 4 'Noise-aware acceptance'; Scope 'an ADR and a contributor guide section'
scenarios: The ADR/contributor guide asserts a bespoke noise-band acceptance rule without acknowledging comparable established methods, inviting a 'why not use X' challenge at review time.
A known reliability pitfall already catalogued in the external literature is re-discovered late rather than designed around.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assign ownership of the `rebar.llm.evals.plan_replay` `__main__`/subcommand dispatcher to one child (e.g. the corpus builder or Tier-0 harness).
evidence: Parent Scope: 'a `python -m rebar.llm.evals.plan_replay` entry'
Child 471c Scope: only `__init__.py`, `corpus.py`
Children 5d19/53ab/f1d6/4c80 all invoke `python -m rebar.llm.evals.plan_replay tier0|tier1|tier2|ledger ...` in their ACs but none lists a `__main__.py`/dispatcher in Scope.
findings.finding: No child owns the package-level CLI dispatcher `python -m rebar.llm.evals.plan_replay` (the entry point the parent Scope and multiple children invoke via `tier0`/`tier1`/`tier2`/`ledger` subcommands). Child 471c creates only `__init__.py`; each tier/ledger child adds its own module but none defines the `__main__`/subcommand dispatch that routes to them.
scenarios: Each tier child's AC references `python -m rebar.llm.evals.plan_replay tierN` but the argument-parsing/subcommand-dispatch module is in no child's file_impact, so the command line cannot resolve subcommands until some unowned integration work happens.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `__main__.py` (or CLI dispatch) to child 471c's or child 5d19's Scope and name it as the owner of subcommand routing.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether child 98df belongs under this epic; if so, list it in the child decomposition and map it to a parent AC, else re-parent it.
